portInfo.description: Portland’s cruise landings sit on the downtown waterfront. The Cruise Portland Maine industry page (City of Portland waterfront contact listed) publishes critical terminal data: capacity framing up to 1,100′ vessels and up to 5,000 passengers, with separate specs for Portland Ocean Terminal and Ocean Gateway Berths 1 and 2. Guest services listed include visitor information, comfort station, on-site restrooms, free Wi-Fi, taxis and public transport, with Maine Medical Center/Mercy Hospital at 1.5 miles and Portland International Jetport at 7 miles. Berth assignment is call-specific — confirm Ocean Gateway vs Portland Ocean Terminal on the day’s schedule before planning a tight museum itinerary.

climate.description: Mediterranean climate with wet winters and dry summers

politics.visaRequirements: Visa-free for citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries (ESTA required). Others need visa.
politics.entryRequirements: Valid passport required. ESTA required for visa-free countries. Some nationalities need visa.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Ask which berth (Ocean Gateway 1/2 vs Portland Ocean Terminal) is assigned before setting a walking clock — lengths and gangway heights differ in the industry FAQ.
